title: Elon Musk Says ‘No Crying in the Casino’ After Broadcom CEO Warns AI Frenzy Is Getting Out of Hand
source_used: Yahoo Finance (Benzinga) for Tan's remarks, ABAB News for Musk's reply; Barron's headline
key_facts: Hock Tan, chief executive of Broadcom, told an event in Singapore on Monday 12 Oct that 'a lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in' (Bloomberg, relayed by Benzinga on Yahoo Finance).
Tan said investors were setting 'very extreme expectations' and found that investing in AI was 'almost like they are in a casino'.
He also compared companies experimenting with AI to children burning through arcade tokens without learning anything.
Tan said access to financing, not memory chip shortages, could become the industry's biggest constraint; our 12 Oct edition carried Reuters on that point.
Elon Musk replied 'No crying in the casino' (Barron's and Benzinga headlines; ABAB News gives the quote in its text).
Barron's text could not be opened (HTTP 401); Benzinga's own page is blocked by Cloudflare.
quote_evidence: 'A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in,' Tan said at an event in Singapore, Bloomberg reported.
He said investors were setting 'very extreme expectations,' only to discover that investing in AI was 'almost like they are in a casino.'
Elon Musk responded to the discussion by saying, 'No crying in the casino.'
why_it_matters_hint: A one-line reply from a prominent tech chief adds attention, not evidence, to the debate over whether AI spending has run ahead of returns.
event_date: Tan's remarks: Monday 12 Oct 2026; Musk's reply: reported 12-13 Oct 2026.
notes: Barron's blocked (401). The Tan side was read on Yahoo Finance (Benzinga) and the Musk quote on ABAB News, a small aggregator; Musk's own post was not opened, so its exact wording and time rest on the Barron's and Benzinga headlines and ABAB News. Follow-up of the 12 Oct 2026 edition's Reuters item on Tan (pool id 1012:C05-05).
